decisive_items: an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure
an abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery
The third portion of the duodenum was not seen in its expected location
response.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings suggest a congenital anomaly of intestinal rotation, which is most consistent with malrotation of the intestine. The abnormal position of the transverse colon, right colic flexure, and superior mesenteric artery-vein relationship support this diagnosis.

rejected.why: The lack of ischemia and normal appendix make intestinal volvulus less likely.
The normal appearance of the appendix on imaging contradicts the diagnosis of acute appendicitis.
